chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from whoever informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the (regular) days of a woman (of menstruation) are ten days, she does not need to examine herself (beyond them); and when they are fewer, she should examine herself.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman's (regular) days — her established habitual menstrual cycle
key_terms.اسْتَظْهَرَتْ: istizhar — the act of cautiously examining oneself beyond one's regular menstrual days to determine if bleeding has continued; a technical fiqhi procedure for women whose cycle may extend
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days — the maximum limit of haydh (menstruation) in Shia jurisprudence; blood beyond this is classified as istihadha

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a woman examining herself during menstruation when her regular cycle is ten days versus fewer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a jurisprudential rule about menstruation (haydh): a woman whose habitual cycle is exactly ten days — the maximum limit for haydh in Shia fiqh — does not need to examine herself beyond that period. However, if her cycle is shorter than ten days and blood continues, she must practice istizhar (cautious examination) to determine whether she is still in haydh or has transitioned to istihadha (non-menstrual bleeding). This ruling reflects the Imami legal framework distinguishing between women of established habit versus those needing to confirm their status.
word_analysis: she should examine herself (beyond her regular days)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the (regular) days (of the menstruation (Haydh) of the woman are ten days, she would not examine herself, and when it was less, she should examine herself’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from those who narrated to him who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If normal duration of a woman’s blood discharge due to Hayd (menses) is ten days, she does not need to perform an examination but if it is less, she must perform an examination.’”
